summary: The patch changes SSTable.delete() in src/java/org/apache/cassandra/io/sstable/SSTable.java so it captures each component's last-modified time once, sorts the components oldest first, and deletes in that order. This matches the ticket's stated fix area (CASSANDRA-21649, bug fix, 4.0 base). Two problems. First, the caller in SSTableTidier (LogTransaction.java:396) still deletes DATA unconditionally before calling SSTable.delete(), so the DATA-first ordering the ticket identifies as the cause is still there whenever Data.db is not the oldest file. Second, the rewrite silently changed error handling: every component now goes through FileUtils.delete(String), which discards the File.delete() result, where the old code used deleteWithConfirm and threw FSWriteError on failure. The ticket's test plan (additions to LogTransactionTest) is not in the patch. No security surface touched. No .claude/, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md edits. Review-only: no tests run.

findings.rule: ticket: SSTableTidier must not delete files out of last-modified order (CASSANDRA-21649 steps 3-5)
findings.problem: The tidier (LogTransaction.java:395-401) calls delete(datafile) on Data.db before SSTable.delete(). The new timestamp-ordered loop in SSTable.delete() therefore never sees DATA. If Data.db holds the newest mtime, it is removed first, the max timestamp changes, and a crash mid-deletion makes LogFile.verifyRecord() reject the REMOVE record on restart, so the node does not start. The patch fixes only the non-DATA ordering that the ticket calls out as secondary. Confidence is medium because I did not verify which file is typically newest in each sstable format.
findings.fix: Remove the unconditional DATA delete in the tidier and let SSTable.delete() order all components by mtime, or apply the same sort to the DATA file inside the tidier. Add a LogTransactionTest case where Data.db is the newest file.

findings.rule: Error handling: no swallowed failures (standards item 30; deleteWithConfirm semantics for sstable components)
findings.problem: Before the patch, DATA and the other components used FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError on failure, so the tidier's catch (Throwable) adds the task to failedDeletions for retry. The patch sends every component through FileUtils.delete(String) (FileUtils.java:545-549), which returns File.delete()'s boolean and the caller ignores it. A failed delete now returns normally, the tidier releases the parent ref and completes the transaction, and the remaining files are leaked with no retry in this process. The SUMMARY component was already lenient, so the strictness loss now also covers DATA and the other components.
findings.fix: Keep the strict path: call FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) in the loop, as the pre-patch code did for every component except SUMMARY. Or check the boolean and throw FSWriteError when it is false.

findings.rule: ticket: Test and documentation plan ('additions to LogTransactionTest')
findings.problem: The ticket's test plan asks for additions to LogTransactionTest. The patch adds no tests and touches only SSTable.java, so the planned regression coverage for the restart and REMOVE-verification scenario is missing.
findings.fix: Add LogTransactionTest cases that delete an sstable with a non-monotonic component mtime set, simulate a partial deletion, and check that the REMOVE timestamp check still passes on restart.
